Subject: Re: P0: Latency + 5xx surge — initial triage and recommended actions

Sergio / team —

Quick triage summary (observed in the last 15m):
- Primary signal: K/V cache pressure on US-EAST-2 inference pool (kb-cache miss rate spiked) causing increased token fetch latency and queuing.
- Metrics: token queue depth peaked at ~420, avg p95 response time 6.8s, backend OOM events reported on 3 nodes (OOM killer triggered after model load peaks).
- Error profile: ~72% of 5xx are 502 gateway/timeout while some others are model execution failures.

Proposed immediate remediation (order matters):
1) Short-term: initiate geo-evac of Northbridge routing to US-WEST-2 with an 80/20 split (west/east) and monitor error rate for 10 minutes. This is the fastest path to reduce user-impact.
2) Concurrent: spin up 4 additional dedicated inference instances (us-west-2 pool) and pre-warm KV caches with a warmup prefix set (we have scripts ready).
3) Fallback: if model memory pressure continues, enable model-fallback to redwood-small-q4 on a per-route basis for 30 minutes. Note: this can slightly change outputs; expected token cost down by ~22%.
4) Post-evac: drain affected us-east-2 nodes, run cache cleanup, and run a controlled model-restart to clear transient memory fragmentation.

Risks & ask: cross-region reroute requires routing policy change with exec-level approval because it touches capacity billing and may require a temporary cross-region SLA exception. We also need Marcus (engineering) on standby for rollbacks if output quality regresses after model-fallback.

Attaching operational runbook: evac_runbook.pdf (runbook excerpt). I'm kicking off the JIRA ticket now (SUP-98765).

Hannah Schmitt
On-call SRE — Redwood Inference
